message.content:
I have the full kernel source and problem contract; I'll record a structured description with the risk surfaces for Skeptic.

Key observations to encode:
- FP16 input widened to FP32; computes u = 1+x exactly in FP32 (FP16→FP32 widening plus 1.0 addition is exact), so correction = (x-(u-1))/u ≈ 0 — the algorithmic surface is the polynomial and range reduction.
- Mantissa kept in [1,2) then halved to [0.5,1)? Actually upper>1.5 halves to (0.75,1), so m∈[0.5,1.5) roughly; z=(m-1)/(m+1) with |z|<1/3. Degree-5-ish polynomial (1+s(1/3 s+...)) with rounded constants 0.142857, 0.2, 0.33333 and split ln2 = 0.69313812256 + 0.0000090580006145 (sum = 0.69314718057... vs ln2 = 0.69314718056 — fine). Risk: polynomial coefficients are truncated (1/7→0.142857, 1/5→0.2, 1/3→0.33333) and only ~degree 5; tolerance is tight absolute 1e-6 over full domain up to x=65504 (log1p ≈ 11.09). For large x, z can approach... after halving mantissa ∈[1,1.5) or [0.75,1.5)? Let me note risks for Skeptic to test: extreme x (near -1, 65504, subnormals, ±0), correction term, exponent term error at large |exponent| (exponent 15 → high ≈ 10.397 with ~1e-6 granularity of constants), and signed-zero (log1p(-0) should be -0, but abs tolerance makes zeros equivalent — fine).

function.arguments: {"contract_model": "[\"Compute log1p elementwise: target[i] = log(1 + x[i]) in real arithmetic on the exact stored FP16 value, FP32 output on x.device.\", \"Fixed absolute tolerance 1e-6, relative tolerance zero, signed zeros numerically equivalent; must hold for every legal input over the whole domain (single verdict, not per-distribution).\", \"Legal domain: 1D contiguous FP16 tensor, N in [1,131072], every finite FP16 value strictly greater than -1 including signed zeros, subnormals, value just above -1, and 65504; NaN/inf/<=-1 excluded.\", \"Input is ordinary Tensor on CUDA, requires_grad=False, non-inference; validate_inputs enforces domain and is called by run; reference is FP64 torch.log1p accepting CPU; make_inputs is examples only.\", \"Return a fresh finite FP32 [N] tensor preserving x; no autograd required.\", \"Frozen environment: NVIDIA T4, PyTorch 2.8.0, Triton 3.4.0.\"], \"kernel_model</arg_key><arg_value>[\"Triton kernel loads FP16 x, widens to FP32, computes u = 1.0 + x (exact in FP32 for any FP16 x), and a Kahan-style correction term (x - (u - 1.0)) / u which should be exactly zero here since 1+x rounds exactly in FP32.\", \"Range reduction via bitcast: u split into exponent (encoding>>23 & 255) - 127 and mantissa with implicit bit restored; mantissa>1.5 is halved with exponent incremented, leaving mantissa roughly in [1, 1.5] and z = (m-1)/(m+1) with |z| < 1/5.\", \"log computed as local_log = 2z * odd polynomial P(s) with s = z^2 and truncated constants: 0.142857 (≈1/7), 0.2 (=1/5 exact), 0.33333 (≈1/3), giving a degree-5 approximation of 2*atanh(z).\", \"Exponent part split as high = e * 0.69313812256, low = e * 0.0000090580006145 (two-part ln2); final value = high + (local_log + (low + correction)); stores FP32 result.\", \"run() validates inputs, allocates FP32 output, launches grid cdiv(N,256) with BLOCK=256, num_warps=4, enable_fp_fusion=False; masked loads/stores handle N not a multiple of 256.\", \"validate_inputs rejects inference mode, non-Tensor, non-contiguous/strided layout, grad or view flags, non-CUDA (in run), wrong shape/dtype, and any non-finite or <=-1 value.\"], \"open_questions</arg_key><arg_value>What is the empirically worst-case absolute error across the full FP16 grid (or a dense sweep), and does any coefficient-truncation or accumulation-order effect exceed 1e-6?\", \"Do Triton 3.4 semantics for uint32 shifts, int/float casts, and enable_fp_fusion=False behave exactly as assumed on the T4 (frozen environment)?\", \"Is the fp16 value just above -1 (next after -1) handled within tolerance despite the correction term being zero in this implementation?\"], \"risk_map</arg_key><arg_value>[\"Truncated polynomial coefficients (1/7 -> 0.142857, 1/3 -> 0.33333; only 0.2 exact) and only degree-5 odd polynomial: worst-case series truncation error scales like |z|^7 with |z|<0.2, likely ~1e-7, but Skeptic should verify against the tight 1e-6 absolute tolerance, especially where s = z^2 is largest (mantissa just above 1.5 before halving, i.e. u near 1.5, x near 0.5).\", \"Error growth with magnitude: for large x (up to 65504, log1p ≈ 11.09) the value is built as high + (local_log + (low + correction)); high ≈ e*ln2_hi ~10.4 so an FP32 ulp there is ~1e-6 and summation/cancellation of split-ln2 parts (ln2_hi + ln2_lo = 0.69314718057... vs true ln2 0.693147180559945) plus non-FMA rounding could exceed 1e-6; probe large-magnitude inputs and the ordering of the final sum.\", \"Inputs just above -1: u = 1+x is a tiny positive FP32 (possibly FP16 subnormal x, u can be exactly 1 + tiny where x < 2^-25 rounds u to 1.0); then encoding = 1.0, exponent 0, mantissa 1.0, z = 0, local_log 0, correction 0 — output 0 instead of log(x) ≈ x; check whether FP16 x magnitude (>= ~5.96e-8 for subnormals, or smallest normal 6.1e-5) keeps |log1p(x) - 0| <= 1e-6.\", \"Signed zeros and -0 handling: log1p(-0) mathematically -0; kernel returns 0 or tiny correction; contract says signed zeros equivalent, so this should be fine, but Skeptic should confirm no NaN/inf path.\", \"Correction term: since 1.0 + x is exact in FP32 for FP16 x, correction is always exactly 0 (or should be); if enable_fp_fusion semantics or the div_rn of (0/u) behave unexpectedly, output near x≈0 could drift; verify numerically near-zero inputs.\", \"Mantissa-halving boundary exactly at mantissa == 1.5: upper uses strict >, so m == 1.5 keeps z = 0.2/2.5 = 0.2 (max |z|); the polynomial accuracy at z = 0.2 is the stress point for the truncation risk above.\", \"Domain enforcement gaps: validate_inputs uses torch.isfinite & x > -1.0 in FP16, matching the contract; but contiguous views with nonzero storage offset are said legal and x.is_contiguous() permits them — the kernel indexes from the view start, which is correct for Triton pointer arithmetic; confirm no offset mishandling.\"], \"scope_notes</arg_key><arg_value>Domain is FP16-only inputs; FP32/FP64 inputs and autograd/inference-mode calls are out of scope.\", \"Tolerance is fixed absolute 1e-6 with zero relative tolerance, so evaluation must be worst-case over the entire legal FP16 domain, not average over make_inputs distributions (which span [-0.75, 3.25]).\", \"reference() is FP64 torch.log1p and accepts CPU inputs; it is the ground truth oracle, so numeric comparison can be done exactly (FP16 inputs make exhaustive or near-exhaustive sweeps feasible: only ~15k positive-domain values plus negatives > -1).\", \"N up to 131072 with BLOCK=256 is a single kernel launch; masking is straightforward and out-of-bounds stores are masked.\", \"No tests directory or test code present in the artifact; correctness must be established via the run/reference contract.\"], \"summary</arg_key><arg_value>case_165: FP16->FP32 elementwise log1p via Triton with mantissa/exponent range reduction, a degree-5 odd polynomial in atanh-style z, split ln2 constants, and a Kahan-style correction term; contract requires abs error <= 1e-6 across all finite FP16 inputs > -1."}
